subject: Performance evaluation protocol & scaling runbook for Globex POC
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@globex.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: ProdOps Team <prodops@globex.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Initial perf questionnaire for POC — baseline & scaling needs

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As we scope the POC, our engineering team asked for a detailed performance questionnaire so we can plan lab time and procurement. We need a clear testing protocol that covers:

- Baseline latency (cold-cache) and steady-state (warmed KV cache) for short (16 tokens) and long (512 tokens) sequences.
- Tail-latency targets (p95/p99/p999) and how these change under autoscale.
- Throughput scaling characteristics (QPS vs GPUs/replicas) and expected headroom.
- Test harness requirements: driver, traffic model (poisson vs burst), dataset (inference prompt corpus), and metrics output.
- Multi-region failover behavior and consistency when routing between regions.
- Any known caveats (quantization, streaming vs non-streaming, prefix cache warmup).

Can you provide a questionnaire or runbook and an estimate of how long each phase will take? We'll likely run a 2–3 day lab window and want to allocate resources accordingly. If you can share sample load scripts and a drive link to the runbook that would be great.

Also include any constraints for the POC account access you need (auth, test data injection, firewall IPs).

Regards,
Sarah Lin
Senior ProdOps Manager, Globex
[sarah.lin@globex.com]

[Attachment: globex_perf_questions.docx]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@globex.com>
Cc: ProdOps Team <prodops@globex.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial perf questionnaire for POC — baseline & scaling needs

Hi Sarah — thanks, this is helpful. Attached is our proposed runbook and the load scripts we use for reproducible runs. High-level plan below; the runbook (redwood_perf_runbook_v1.pdf) has full step-by-step commands and expected outputs.

Summary of phases (recommended):
1) Cold-start baseline (2–3 hours): single replica, cold KV/cache, measure p50/p95/p99 for 16/128/512 token prompts. Purpose: quantify kernel startup + KV population impact.
2) Warmed steady-state (4–6 hours): steady QPS ramps to target, KV cache pre-warmed. Measure sustained throughput, per-token cost, and tail-latency under continuous load.
3) Autoscale ramp and burst tests (3–4 hours): simulated traffic spikes (Poisson + sudden burst) to validate autoscale policies and assess p99 behavior during scale events.
4) Capacity sweep (3–6 hours): scale replicas/GPUs and record QPS vs replicas to derive linearity coefficient and headroom.
5) Multi-region failover (2 hours): route traffic between us-west/us-east, measure latency and error behavior during routing and DB/metrics convergence.

Key metrics we will provide: p50/p90/p95/p99/p999 latencies, requests/sec, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory/KV hit ratio, cold vs warm delta, error rates, and percent of requests served from cache. We also output flamegraphs/trace links for any ops regressions.

Caveats and notes:
- Quantized model variants may show different tail-latency; we recommend testing the exact model variant you intend to serve in production.
- Streaming RPC adds ~10–30ms overhead at small token sizes but improves perceived latency for long streams.
- KV cache warmup matters: we include a small warmup driver that pre-populates common prefixes; we recommend including it if you plan to serve chat with long histories.

Attachments included: redwood_perf_runbook_v1.pdf, load-scripts-v2.tar.gz, kv-warmup-checklist.md. Also sharing a Drive link with example result artifacts after the run.

If this aligns, propose Wed–Thu next week for the lab window. I can set up a scoped POC token and temporary IP allowlist — we'll need the CIDR you want to use and a test S3 bucket (or we can host prompts).

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
[vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com]

[Attachment stubs: redwood_perf_runbook_v1.pdf (26 pages), load-scripts-v2.tar.gz (12 scripts), kv-warmup-checklist.md]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: quick alignment on Globex run parameters

Marissa/Karthik — looping you both in to finalize targets for the Globex POC run. Notes from Sarah below and my proposed defaults. Please confirm or flag concerns.

Proposed test matrix:
- Sequences: 16, 128, 512 tokens (use their anonymized prompt set).
- Target steady QPS: 250–500 r/s initial; capacity sweep up to 2k r/s.
- Target latencies to validate: p95 < 180ms (16 tokens), p95 < 350ms (128 tokens), p95 < 650ms (512 tokens) on dedicated x2 A100-equivalent GPUs per replica.
- Autoscale policy: add replica at 70% GPU util sustained for 30s; remove at <50% for 60s.

Questions for you:
1) Marissa — do we need an explicit cold-cache baseline longer than 2 hours to capture kernel JIT effects?
2) Karthik — any recommended batch sizes for 512 token runs to balance latency vs throughput (we had good results with batching=2/4 on quantized runs last quarter).

Also, I plan to enable prefix cache pre-warm for the warmed steady-state and capture hit-ratio metrics. We'll annotate traces with model variant and quantization level.

-Vivek

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: quick alignment on Globex run parameters

Vivek — looks good. Two quick points:
- Cold baseline: extend to 4 hours for the 512-token case to be safe — we've seen model graph warming and kernel autotune settle over longer sequences.
- For quantized variants, run both batching=1 and batching=4; that gives us a clean comparison for tail-latency sensitivity.

I'll update the runbook section on measurement tags and prepare a small script to strip PII from their prompt corpus.

-Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@globex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, ProdOps Team <prodops@globex.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial perf questionnaire for POC — baseline & scaling needs

Hi Sarah — attaching the consolidated runbook and scripts as discussed. Highlights and next steps: 

- Attached artifacts: redwood_perf_runbook_v1.pdf (end-to-end protocol), load-scripts-v2.tar.gz (driver + traffic models), kv-warmup-checklist.md (warmup procedure).
- We implemented Marissa's suggestion: cold baseline extended to 4 hours for the 512-token case; runbook notes this under Phase 1.
- We will run the following matrix during the 3-day window: cold-baseline (extended), warmed steady-state, autoscale ramp, capacity sweep, multi-region failover. Expect ~14–16 hours of active test time plus analysis.
- Deliverables: CSV of raw metrics, annotated traces, aggregated SLO table (p50/p90/p95/p99/p999) and a short executive summary with recommended capacity targets and cost estimates.

Request from Globex: can you confirm the test window (proposed Wed 4/21–Thu 4/22), the CIDRs to allowlist for the POC driver (we'll provide our IPs), and a sample of the prompt corpus (anonymized) or an S3 read-only bucket for us to pull prompts?

Related links: results template and example artifacts will be uploaded here after the run: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1perfRunbook. HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/98765 (DEAL-74321). Internal benchmark reference (for our ops): https://internal.redwood.com/benchmarks/run-2026-03-29.

Thanks — Vivek
